directoryStems.mcq-1b9947447ef263b529e44bd0: בת 82, עצמאית ב- BADL וללא חסר קוגניטיבי. סובלת מסוכרת בשנים האחרונות. ברקע ידוע על אי ספיקת כליות קלה. המטופלת מעוניינת לדעת אילו ערכים מומלצים לה לפי הקווים המנחים, שפורסמו לאחרונה (מאמר SDANDARTS OF MEDICAL CARE 2020).
directoryStems.mcq-90bbae3292be580263244c30: בת 77, פנתה לבדיקה שגרתית. מדובר בפנייה ראשונה למרפאה מזה כ-10 שנים. בבדיקות דם שביצעה לפני כשבוע, שלא בצום, סוכר 184 מ"ג/ד"ל, המוגלובין A1C- 6.2%. האם מדובר בסוכרת?
directoryStems.mcq-eab9b27c6d0193e1d23c6a83: איזה גורם פיזיולוגי מעלה סיכון להיפוגליקמיה בגיל המבוגר?
directoryStems.mcq-5e41e7a32048963dcee0a671: בת 84, עצמאית בתפקודה וללא ירידה קוגניטיבית ידועה. ברקע סוכרת ויתר לחץ דם. מה צריך לכלול הטיפול בסוכרת על פי המאמר Older Adults: Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes 2020?
directoryStems.mcq-1dddbf5cbecf18ddb2743abe: Which glucose-lowering drug class has cardiovascular and kidney benefits described by Hazzard in older adults, while requiring caution about genital infections and diabetic ketoacidosis?
directoryStems.mcq-7b61f10b0e09da43b7a59bc6: A 79-year-old woman with diabetes and declining vision is diagnosed with center-involved diabetic macular edema. Which treatment approach is consistent with Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-b2ef7c80a13e0d976cc232e2: A 66-year-old man reports four months of progressive erectile dysfunction. He has no known medical history but has lost about 18 kg over six months and reports polyuria, polydipsia, fatigue, and mood changes. Which interpretation of the metabolic symptom cluster follows Hazzard's description of diabetes in older adults?
directoryStems.mcq-763d706646a57e21583ac6eb: A 73-year-old woman with diabetes is taking metformin and is hospitalized with a major acute illness that may reduce tissue perfusion. Which drug-related concern justifies avoiding metformin in this situation?
directoryStems.mcq-6ce030c1e8e4610eb789c910: A 78-year-old woman with diabetes, depression, and mild Alzheimer dementia attends a geriatric assessment. Her daughter reports missed medications and two hypoglycemic episodes requiring emergency visits. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg twice daily, sertraline 100 mg daily, and donepezil 10 mg daily. HbA1c is 6.8%, and recorded glucose values range from 65 to 280. Which medication change most directly reduces the risk of another sulfonylurea-related hypoglycemic episode?
directoryStems.mcq-5c3438eacbba727a282e1f92: An 83-year-old woman with insulin-treated diabetes and declining kidney function has episodes of hypoglycemia. Which relationship between kidney function and insulin treatment explains the need to review her insulin dose?
directoryStems.mcq-17ca199d22bdf14a9a5ea1e2: A 74-year-old woman with diabetes and HbA1c 7.2% reports dizziness and near-falls. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 5 mg daily, and lisinopril 10 mg daily, and recently began tramadol 50 mg three times daily for osteoarthritis pain. Pre-lunch glucose values are 68–75 mg/dL. When reviewing glipizide because of concern about hypoglycemia, which statement follows Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-627ff19f2b46bf76ced241ee: A woman taking metformin is hospitalized with a severe acute illness that reduces tissue perfusion. Which risk explains avoiding metformin in this setting?
directoryStems.mcq-597d54ec6ba3081d6aa9a32a: During medication review for an older adult with recurrent hypoglycemia, which glucose-lowering drug class does Hazzard advise avoiding when hypoglycemia is a concern?
directoryStems.mcq-d84fad091b9595eb8a034c32: A 76-year-old with cognitive impairment forgets tablets and takes glyburide 10 mg twice daily and metformin. Her A1C is 9.2% and creatinine clearance is 48 mL/min. Which step should guide the next treatment plan?
directoryStems.mcq-00ff881c7510535484e23172: An 84-year-old man with diabetes, stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73 m²) and mild cognitive impairment attends the emergency department after a fall. His daughter reports three falls in the last month and increasing confusion. His medications are metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily and zolpidem 10 mg nightly. Blood pressure is 108/65 seated and 92/58 standing; heart rate rises from 72 to 74. Creatinine is 2.8 and glucose is 68. Which action regarding metformin is supported by his renal function?
directoryStems.mcq-e40c3f4c851834c19e96ae49: A 76-year-old woman with diabetes and mild cognitive impairment has recurrent hypoglycemia while taking metformin, glipizide, and insulin according to glucose readings. The acute episode has been treated. Her eGFR is stable at 38 mL/min/1.73 m2, without acute illness or impaired perfusion. What should be the focus of medication adjustment to prevent recurrence?
directoryStems.mcq-68fbd246fe9af04028418e22: A 72-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and recently diagnosed mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 22/30) receives home-based primary care. Her daughter found her unconscious twice in the past month, both times early in the morning before breakfast. She takes glimepiride 4 mg once daily with breakfast, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 10 mg daily. Her latest HbA1c is 6.8%, creatinine clearance is 58 mL/min, and prebreakfast fingerstick glucose readings range from 68 to 95 mg/dL. Which approach to the sulfonylurea agrees with Hazzard when hypoglycemia is a concern?
directoryStems.mcq-7771823681e97f4145063540: A 77-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and moderate Alzheimer dementia lives with her daughter, who has discovered medication errors. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glyburide 10 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, donepezil 10 mg daily, and aspirin 81 mg daily. HbA1c is 7.2%, blood pressure is 145/85, and eGFR is 48. Which statement correctly identifies the source-described hypoglycemia concern in her oral diabetes regimen?
directoryStems.mcq-a5fda5af306b5794a9507532: A 79-year-old woman with diabetes takes metformin. Her eGFR has fallen to 28 mL/min/1.73 m². Considering the renal appropriateness of metformin separately from treatment of congestion, which action follows Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-11e41b3874eda173c1930b02: An 81-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and stage 3a chronic kidney disease (eGFR 48 mL/min/1.73 m²) is assessed before elective hip replacement. He takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, and aspirin 81 mg. Preoperative tests show creatinine 1.8 mg/dL, potassium 4.2, and glucose 156. He lives alone and manages his medications, but his daughter reports that he has recently been forgetting appointments. Which principle should guide the metformin safety review around surgery?
directoryStems.mcq-3b5b33f466553786f738f776: A 78-year-old man with frailty (Clinical Frailty Scale 6), heart failure (ejection fraction 35%), and stage 4 chronic kidney disease (eGFR 22) attends follow-up. HbA1c is 7.2%, potassium 4.8, and creatinine 2.8. Which change addresses the metformin contraindication stated in Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-8fc5cd5a3c33775082ac9141: Which result in older Diabetes Prevention Program participants supports counseling about lifestyle intervention?
directoryStems.mcq-f902278ecd62cedaf676906a: A 78-year-old man has type 2 diabetes, hypertension, COPD, and stage 3 CKD (eGFR 45 mL/min). He takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glyburide 10 mg daily, lisinopril 40 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, tiotropium, and simvastatin 20 mg daily. He reports two falls on standing in the past month; HbA1c is 7.2%, and blood pressure falls from 128/76 sitting to 108/68 standing. Separate evaluation of the falls is planned. Which medication change best reduces hypoglycemia risk in this patient?
directoryStems.mcq-d4f9a0dcdc4fcb88e86475eb: An older woman in rehabilitation takes glipizide and has documented hypoglycemic episodes during poor oral intake. After the episodes are treated, which principle should guide continued use of the drug?
directoryStems.mcq-9f0f15a011392bd47e967318: An 80-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and mild dementia has weight loss and frequent falls. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 40 mg, and aspirin 81 mg. BMI fell from 23 to 19 over 8 months; HbA1c is 6.4% and LDL is 68. She forgets meals and struggles with cooking. Grip strength is 14 kg, and she rises slowly while holding furniture. Which adjustment addresses the hypoglycemia risk emphasized by Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-5c872bf476c30d9b0cd38ec9: A 76-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and cognitive impairment needs treatment intensification. He forgets medications and meals and lives alone. Before selecting an insulin regimen for home use, which planning approach follows Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-ad143b0d3e896f3874a20638: An older adult treated with insulin develops impaired vision and hand dexterity. Before selecting a self-monitoring device, what should be assessed according to Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-53d73bf4c0a4e3dc615c8cd4: An older adult with stable type 2 diabetes is being considered for oral treatment. There is no acute illness, unstable heart failure, or renal contraindication. Which statement describes the principal glucose-lowering action of metformin in Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-b476cea9057460b2d0c4589d: A 75-year-old woman with early Alzheimer disease (MMSE 24) and diabetes attends a routine review. She lives alone, drives short distances, and uses a pillbox filled weekly by her daughter. HbA1c is 9.2%, compared with 7.8% six months earlier. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily and glipizide 10 mg twice daily. Her daughter has found glucose tablets around the home and reports morning shakiness. During a review of possible hypoglycemia, which change removes a hypoglycemia-risk drug while individualizing her treatment goals?
directoryStems.mcq-d06967371079047bbb34729f: An 81-year-old with stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22) is under observation for an acute subdural hematoma. Oral intake is unpredictable and glucose is persistently 250–300 mg/dL. She takes metformin and glipizide. Which inpatient plan best limits medication-related harm while treating hyperglycemia?
directoryStems.mcq-e25e4aabace92dfb737c4053: An 81-year-old man with diabetes fell during documented hypoglycemia. His oral glucose-lowering therapy is being reviewed to reduce further episodes. Which listed drug belongs to a class with a significant risk of hypoglycemia?
directoryStems.mcq-15e4b324e152d5041f2781f1: A 78-year-old woman with diabetes and mild dementia lives alone. Her A1C is 9.2% on metformin; she forgets medications and meals. Her daughter requests insulin, but the patient does not want injections. Her MMSE is 28/30, although medication tasks require prompting. After reviewing her goals and arranging adherence support, an oral DPP-4 inhibitor is being discussed. Which description of this drug class matches Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-856e86b9c57bee66f48576de: An 81-year-old woman with diabetes receives insulin and a beta-blocker for cardiovascular disease. Which beta-blocker effect is relevant to hypoglycemia safety?
directoryStems.mcq-ab0a6a05e5bd42256ebbb5c8: An older patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease takes metformin and has an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 32 mL/min/1.73 m². Which monitoring principle is consistent with Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-0a7d2295767fba949e6d8c2d: An older adult on metformin develops an acute illness with hypoxemia and worsening renal perfusion. Which medication action is appropriate during the acute episode?
directoryStems.mcq-08365612ee9cd565c6be52ce: A 76-year-old man with diabetes taking metformin develops a severe acute illness with tissue hypoperfusion around the time of surgery. What is the main reason to avoid metformin in this situation?
directoryStems.mcq-9de46a38d6118487095e423f: An 84-year-old woman who often misses meals has a severe hypoglycemic episode while taking glipizide and metformin. After immediate correction, repeat renal testing shows a stable eGFR of 27 mL/min/1.73 m². Which plan addresses both medication hazards?
directoryStems.mcq-04182e576b08982e7e75a1af: בן 75, עצמאי ב- BADL. ברקע - סכרת ואי ספיקת לב, מטופל ב- DAPAGLIFUZIN (FORXIGA), LINAGLIPTIN (TRAJENTA), METFORMIN, ENALAPRIL ו- DISOTHIAZIDE. התקבל לאשפוז אלקטיבי לניתוח TKR שבוצע ללא אירועים חריגים. ביממה השנייה לאחר הניתוח חלה ירידה במצב ההכרה, החולה נמצא ישנוני ומבולבל. ל"ד 90/60 דופק 100 סדיר, סטורציה תקינה, חום תקין. במעבדה: בדיקה ויחידות ערך לחולה ערכי נורמה BUN mg/dL 80 25 - 5 CREATININE mg/dL 1.7 0.6-1.1 NA mmol/L 145 135-146 K mmol/L 4.5 3.5-5.3 Cl mmol/L 88 95-110 PH 7.0 7.35-7.45 PCO2 mmHg 35 35-46 HCO3 mmol/L 14 21-26 בבדיקת שתן: לויקוציטים +, תאים אדומים -, ניטריט -, קטונים +++ תופעת לוואי של איזו מהתרופות הבאות עשויה להיות הגורם למצבו של החולה?
directoryStems.mcq-56a18f5157de81e337b3769d: בן 78, מתגורר עם מטפל זר. ברקע סוכרת, יתר לחץ דם, מחלת לב איסכמית, מצב לאחר אירוע מוחי איסכמי עם חולשת צד ימין קלה, דמנציה מתקדמת, נזקק לעזרה בכל צרכי ה- ADL. אושפז במחלקה פנימית עקב אורוספסיס. בקבלתו לאשפוז HbA1C- 9.5%. הותחל טיפול ב- INSULIN. בני המשפחה הודרכו לגבי טיפול באינסולין. מה ההמלצות להמשך טיפול בסוכרת לפי המאמר Older Adults: Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes—2020?
directoryStems.mcq-7df358e819f02b4a8d3dd0d7: בן 87, סובל מסוכרת שנים רבות. מזה שנתיים ללא טיפול תרופתי. ברקע – מחלת אלצהיימר, גר עם מטפל צמוד ומתנייד עם הליכון. המטפל מדווח שהמטופל מרבה לשתות ומטיל שתן בתכיפות גדולה. ירד במשקל 6 ק"ג בחודשים האחרונים. במעבדה המוגלובין A1C – 11%. על פי המאמר ADA Older Adults: Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes-2022 מה הטיפול המומלץ?
directoryStems.mcq-e3682940da67f696841ee7d2: בן 75, ברקע מחלת לב איסכמית, אי-ספיקת כליות עם GFR של 45 מ"ל/דקה, אירוע של CVA בעבר. במעבדה – המוגלובין A1C – 8.9%. לאיזו מהתרופות הבאות לסוכרת יש פוטנציאל להביא לשינוי פרוגנוסטי למחלות הרקע?
directoryStems.mcq-8180581eed958ca16d78940c: בן 75, שמור קוגניטיבית ועצמאי בתפקודו, סובל מסוכרת מאז גיל 50. ברקע מחלת לב איסכמית עם סטנט ל-LAD לפני כעשור ואי-ספיקת כליות כרונית עם GFR של 52 מ"ל/דקה. המטופל שוקל 80 ק"ג (BMI 28). תרופות: INSULIN LANTUS 18 units+ APIDRA 6 units X3, RAMIPRIL, ATORVASTATIN, METFORMIN, ASPIRIN, EMPAGLYFLOZIN. במעבדה: פאנל שומנים בדם- LDL 68, HDL 34, Triglycerides 124 המוגלובין A1C -7.0 יחס אלבומין-קריאטינין 357 על פי המאמר ADA Older Adults: Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes-2022 איזה מבין השינויים התרופתיים הבאים יועיל למטופל?
directoryStems.mcq-f603c1f000f2b50035e3edce: על פי מחקר ה- Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP) בארה"ב, איזה מהבאים נכון בנוגע לדרכים למניעת סוכרת בגיל המבוגר?

directoryStems.mcq-2d266bac558345e208370988:
בן 80, שמור קוגניטיבית ועצמאי בתפקוד, BMI = 30, ברקע מחלת לב איסכמית עם צנתור אחרון לפני כעשור, אי ספיקת כליות עם קריאטנין 1.7 (EGFR של 40 מ"ל/דקה). טיפול תרופתי קבוע:  
 INSULIN GLARGINE (LANTUS) 22IU x 1/day  
 RAMIPRIL 5 mg x 1/d

 MICROPIRIN 100 mg x 1/d  
 תוצאות מעבדה: מדד ויחידות החולה ערכים תקינים LDL mg/dL 95 <100 HDL mg/dL 32 >40 Triglycerides mg/dL 101 <150 HBA1C % 8.2 <5.7 Albumin/Creatinine mg/g 300 <30 מה מבין השינויים התרופתיים הבאים הוא בעל אפקט פרוגנוסטי חיובי למטופל?

directoryStems.mcq-c2279ef45642c96c7994044f: מה נכון מבחינת סיבוכי מחלת הסוכרת?
directoryStems.mcq-00447e6d3dddf948ba023322: בן 72 מאובחן עם סוכרת סוג 2, מגיע למרפאתך לייעוץ בנוגע לניהול אורח חיים. המטופל מעוניין בהתחלת תוכנית פעילות גופנית על פי המלצת ה- American Diabetes Association (ADA), איזה מההנחיות הבאות מומלצת עבורו?
directoryStems.mcq-05fcd2cc3d52e4ec75c5cf4b:
בת 71, עצמאית בתפקוד וניידות. נמצאת במעקב מרפאת סוכרת 4 שנים. הגיעה למרפאה לביקור, HBA1C = 7.4%, לא ידוע על אירועי היפוגליצמיה. מקבלת טיפול ב:  
 Insulin Toujeo 16 units X 1  
 T.Jardiance 10 mg x 1  
 T.Glucomin 850 mg x 1  
 מה חשוב להמליץ בביקור במרפאה?
directoryStems.mcq-25bc482e2e15dfa244621080: בת 85 עם סוכרת סוג 2 מזה 15 שנה, מתגוררת במוסד סיעודי. ברקע: מחלת לב כלילית, אי ספיקת לב, מחלת כליות כרונית שלב 3, ודמנציה בדרגה בינונית. זקוקה לעזרה בפעילויות יומיומיות. HbA1c עדכני 8.1% תחת טיפול ב- JARDIANCE מה הוא הטיפול המתאים עבורה?

highlightAliases.old: 3 tiers by comorbidity/function/cognition: Good, Intermediate, Poor health.
highlightAliases.new: 3 tiers by comorbidity/function/cognition: Good, Intermediate, Poor health; Current practice (not the book): individualize targets (grade C): healthy older adults with few stable illnesses and intact cognition/function should have lower goals such as A1C <7.0-7.5% and/or CGM time in 70-180 mg/dL ≥70% and time ≤70 mg/dL ≤4%; complex/intermediate health prioritizes hypoglycemia avoidance, with less stringent goals such as A1C <8.0%, time in 70-180 mg/dL ≥50% and time <70 mg/dL <1%, considering cognition/function, frailty, comorbidity, medication risk-benefit and preferences; very complex/poor health avoids reliance on A1C and focuses on avoiding hypoglycemia and symptomatic hyperglycemia, with no numerical CGM goal specified; fasting/premeal and bedtime ranges respectively are 80-130/80-180 mg/dL (healthy), 90-150/100-180 (complex/intermediate) and 100-180/110-200 (very complex/poor); lower A1C goals require no recurrent/severe hypoglycemia or undue treatment burden - ADA Standards of Care 2026, Section 13, recommendations 13.7a-c pS282 and Table 13.2 pS284

highlightAliases.old: Sulfonylureas (e.g., glipizide 2.5–10 mg qd–BID) (p1577). Cautions: hypoglycemia; avoid glyburide — long half-life, not recommended in older adults (p1579); avoid in renal/hepatic impairment (p1579).
highlightAliases.new: Sulfonylureas (e.g., glipizide 2.5–10 mg qd–BID) (p1577). Cautions: hypoglycemia; avoid glyburide — long half-life, not recommended in older adults (p1579); avoid in renal/hepatic impairment (p1579); Required reading: see AGS Beers 2023 required-article card for qualified sulfonylurea avoidance and the preference if one is used (Table 2, p2061)

highlightAliases.old: Metformin / metformin ER: printed dose lines 500–1000 mg BID, max 2500 mg/d, 500–2000 mg qd — the page does not pair each line to an agent (p1577). Cautions: avoid if eGFR <30; avoid in unstable heart failure/acute illness (lactic-acidosis risk) (p1576).
highlightAliases.new: Metformin / metformin ER: printed dose lines 500–1000 mg BID, max 2500 mg/d, 500–2000 mg qd — the page does not pair each line to an agent (p1577). Cautions: avoid if eGFR <30; avoid in unstable heart failure or during acute hospitalization for major illness that could reduce tissue perfusion (lactic-acidosis risk) (p1576).

highlightAliases.old: CVD-outcome-proven drug classes (large CVOTs, average participant age >60): SGLT-2 inhibitors (empagliflozin, canagliflozin, dapagliflozin) and GLP-1 agonists (liraglutide, semaglutide, dulaglutide) (p1571).
highlightAliases.new: CVD-outcome-proven drug classes (large CVOTs, average participant age >60): SGLT-2 inhibitors (empagliflozin, canagliflozin, dapagliflozin) and GLP-1 agonists (liraglutide, semaglutide, dulaglutide) (p1570–1571).

highlightAliases.old: Cognitive screening at diagnosis, then annually if borderline or every 2–3 years if normal (p1568).
highlightAliases.new: The chapter gives annual follow-up after a borderline cognitive screen and every 2–3 years after a normal screen (p1568). ADA 2026 recommends an initial screen and annual screening from age 65, with additional assessment when self-management changes.

highlightAliases.old: BP target <140/90 mmHg for most; consider 130/80 mmHg for high-risk (prior stroke, progressing CKD), with orthostatic monitoring (p1572).
highlightAliases.new: Hazzard gives a BP goal below 140/90 mmHg for most (p1572). ADA 2026 recommends below 130/80 mmHg when safely attainable. For poor health, limited life expectancy or high treatment risk, a goal such as below 140/90 may be appropriate. Check standing BP (ADA 2026, recommendation 13.9).
